original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Speed up Git tree authentication in the 92-PR, next-100 and third-100 reconciliation verifiers by reusing an OID only for an identical path, mode and blob listing, while every pinned tree SHA and the rest of each verifier stay in force.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue asks whether one measured replay bottleneck can be sped up without dropping coverage, by source-bound reuse with explicit invalidation. The measured stage is the tree walk inside the three verifiers that scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py runs. The domain is their pinned commit trees and, for the two larger audits, their CI checkout trees. Evidence archives stay byte-identical; only each verifier and its manifest self-pin change.
bottleneck_link: These three verifiers are on the reconciliation path that review replay already runs. A faster tree check with the same pinned SHAs shortens that replay without changing the selected multiplication exponent.
stop_rule: Stop after this one stage. Do not retune gzip or JSON parsing, and do not treat a faster tree OID as a change to kappa. A cached walk that is not faster than the predecessor on the same listings falsifies the change.
evidence: Every pinned tree OID matches the base-commit predecessor and the cached walk. A one-blob edit misses the cache and disagrees with the pin. A poisoned cache fails audit. The three integrated verifiers still pass their other evidence checks.
author: research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used to profile the verifier, implement the cache, and write this package. The assistance is disclosed without naming a coding-agent product.

open_questions.question: Can the residual gzip and JSON cost of these three verifiers be reduced without changing pinned evidence bytes or the manifest self-check?
open_questions.why_it_matters: After the tree cache, most of the remaining wall time is decompression and parsing of the same archives, so review replay is still dominated by that I/O.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one unprofiled third-100 run, separate gzip.decompress from json.loads, and test one reuse keyed by the compressed bytes.
open_questions.blocked_by: A parsed-object cache has to miss when those bytes change, and the manifest still hashes the bytes. This package does not change that path.

open_questions.question: Should each historical manifest pin scripts/git_tree_oid.py so a later edit cannot change tree authentication unnoticed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The verifiers import that helper. Their manifests pin verify.py, not the helper, so a helper edit changes the digest while the self-pin still matches.
open_questions.first_step: Record the helper path and SHA256 in each manifest and reject a one-byte helper change before accepting a tree OID.
open_questions.blocked_by: Those manifests currently list only files inside the audit directory. Extending that inventory is a separate evidence-format change.
